staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged checkout. Metadata records vulnerable commit `ead0756c96ca6f562645a18fe57aa2749d9190e0`, but the local tree's line map matches the saved ASan allocation at `src/server/ua_services_discovery.c:122` and crash at `:136`; this is the exact source traced here.

classification_note: Sample metadata leaves the class `unclassified`. The staged source and saved sanitizer trace show an out-of-bounds heap write caused by missing duplicate-entry filtering in `Service_FindServers`.

bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists where duplicate entries in the filter list are not checked, potentially allowing unintended behavior due to repeated filters.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 458-byte witness is a four-chunk OPC UA SecureConversation stream processed by a fresh server instance. Its first `MSG` chunk decodes as numeric request type id 437 (`RegisterServerRequest_Encoding_DefaultBinary`) and reaches `process_RegisterServer()`, which inserts one registered server entry and increments `server->registeredServersSize` to 1; the stored `serverUri` is a zero-length `UA_String` because the witness encodes that field with a negative UA Binary string length. The later `MSG` chunk decodes as numeric request type id 422 (`FindServersRequest_Encoding_DefaultBinary`) and materializes `serverUrisSize = 2` with both filter entries decoding to the same zero-length `UA_String`. In the fresh fuzz server, `UA_ServerConfig_new_default()` leaves `server->config.applicationDescription.applicationUri` at the non-empty default literal `urn:unconfigured:application`, so both duplicate zero-length filters fail the line-129 self-URI guard and enter the registered-server loop. Vulnerable `Service_FindServers()` allocates `foundServerFilteredPointer` for exactly `registeredServersSize` pointers, i.e. one 8-byte slot. The first duplicate filter entry appends the sole registered server and sets `foundServersSize = 1`; the second duplicate entry matches the same stored `serverUri` again, and because the code does not check whether that server was already recorded before executing `foundServerFilteredPointer[foundServersSize++] = &current->registeredServer`, it writes a second pointer at index 1 past the 1-slot heap buffer. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting 8-byte heap-buffer-overflow write at `src/server/ua_services_discovery.c:136`. The staged patch resolves this by adding an `existing` scan before the append and skipping duplicate filter matches.

evidence_note: The saved `poc` was statically decoded under the staged open62541 UA Binary semantics rather than rerun. That decode confirms the chunk sequence `OPNF(132), MSGF(97), OPNF(132), MSGF(97)`, first-MSG request type id 437, second-MSG request type id 422, and the duplicate zero-length `serverUris` values that drive the overflow.

source.description: First project-code parser step on the crashing witness path. For the first `MSG` chunk, this call materializes the `UA_RegisterServerRequest` fields that seed the server's discovery-state extent and stored URI.
source.value_from: In the exact 458-byte `poc`, the first `MSG` body begins at offset `0x9c` with request-type bytes `01 20 b5 01`, so `processMSG()` dispatches it as numeric id 437 (`RegisterServerRequest_Encoding_DefaultBinary`). Under staged `UA_decodeBinary` semantics, that request decodes `serverUri` as a zero-length `UA_String`, `serverNamesSize = 2`, `discoveryUrlsSize = 1`, and `isOnline = true`.
source.note: Source. This first `UA_decodeBinary` call creates the later discovery-state seed from attacker-controlled bytes. The important materialized value is `request->server.serverUri`: its negative encoded string length is normalized by `Array_decodeBinary` into a zero-length `UA_String` (`length = 0`, `data = NULL`).

tainted_value_origin.statement: retval = UA_decodeBinary(msg, &offset, request, requestType, server->config.customDataTypesSize, server->config.customDataTypes);
tainted_value_origin.description: For the second `MSG` chunk, the same decode statement materializes the duplicate filter array that directly drives both append attempts in `Service_FindServers()`.

It yields `serverUrisSize = 2`, and both encoded `serverUris` entries normalize to the same zero-length `UA_String`.

root_cause.description: The duplicate-match branch treats every matching filter entry as new. It does not check whether that same `serverUri` was already stored in `foundServerFilteredPointer[0..foundServersSize)` before falling through to the append.
root_cause.note: The staged patch adds the missing `existing` scan immediately inside this branch and skips the append when the same filter target is already present.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. The duplicate second append uses `foundServersSize == 1` as the index even though `foundServerFilteredPointer` has capacity for only one pointer.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved ASan report records `heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 8` here, with the overwritten address exactly 0 bytes past the 8-byte allocation created at line 122.

parser_admitted.statement: retval = UA_decodeBinary(msg, &offset, request, requestType, server->config.customDataTypesSize, server->config.customDataTypes);
parser_admitted.description: After the second `MSG` chunk's numeric id 422 dispatch, this successful decode materializes the `UA_FindServersRequest` object that immediately enters `Service_FindServers()`.

fine_trace.note: The harness copies the exact 458-byte PoC into `msg.data`, preserving the four-chunk stream `OPNF(132), MSGF(97), OPNF(132), MSGF(97)`. This single buffer contains the `RegisterServerRequest` body at offset `0x9c` and the later `FindServersRequest` body at offset `0x181`.

Source. For the first `MSG` chunk, whose decoded request type id is numeric 437, this call materializes a `UA_RegisterServerRequest`. The witness encodes `request->server.serverUri` with a negative string length, so `Array_decodeBinary` normalizes it to a zero-length `UA_String` (`length = 0`, `data = NULL`); the same decode yields `serverNamesSize = 2`, `discoveryUrlsSize = 1`, and `isOnline = true`.

On the fresh server instance, `process_RegisterServer()` takes the new online registration path for step 2's decoded request and increments `registeredServersSize` from 0 to 1. This later defines the capacity of `foundServerFilteredPointer`.

The new list entry copies the decoded `requestServer` object. The sole stored registered server therefore carries the same zero-length `serverUri` from step 2, which later `Service_FindServers()` will compare against the filter entries.

Later in the same saved four-chunk witness, a second `processMSG()` invocation decodes the `MSG` body at offset `0x181` as numeric request type id 422 (`FindServersRequest_Encoding_DefaultBinary`). This call materializes `serverUrisSize = 2`; both encoded `serverUris` elements again carry negative lengths, so `UA_decodeBinary` turns them into identical zero-length `UA_String`s (`length = 0`, `data = NULL`).
Because step 5 produced a nonzero `serverUrisSize`, `Service_FindServers()` takes the filtered-search path instead of the unfiltered `self + registered servers` path.

The temporary filter-result array is sized only by the number of registered servers. With step 3's `registeredServersSize == 1`, `fsfpSize` is one pointer and ASan reports the resulting 8-byte allocation at line 122.

On the first filter entry, the self-URI guard is false. The fresh fuzz server uses `UA_ServerConfig_new_default()` -> `UA_ServerConfig_new_minimal()`, which sets `server->config.applicationDescription.applicationUri` to the non-empty default literal `"urn:unconfigured:application"` (`plugins/ua_config_default.c:53,121`); step 5's zero-length `request->serverUris[0]` therefore cannot satisfy this `UA_String_equal` check, so `addSelf` stays `UA_FALSE` and control falls into the registered-server loop.

With step 8 sending control into the `else` arm, the registered-server loop compares the stored zero-length `current->registeredServer.serverUri` from step 4 to step 5's first zero-length filter and matches. This in-bounds append stores `&current->registeredServer` at index 0 and advances `foundServersSize` from 0 to 1.

The second duplicate filter entry reaches the same self-URI guard with `addSelf` still `UA_FALSE`. Step 9 only incremented `foundServersSize`; it did not set `addSelf`, and step 5's `request->serverUris[1]` is the same zero-length string, so the line-129 comparison again fails against the non-empty default `applicationUri`. Control therefore enters the registered-server loop a second time.

Root cause. On this second registered-server loop, the same zero-length filter string matches the same stored registered server again. This branch has no check that the match was already recorded in `foundServerFilteredPointer[0..foundServersSize)`, so the duplicate filter entry still falls through to the append with `foundServersSize == 1`.

Sink. With `foundServersSize == 1` from step 9 and only one allocated slot from step 7, the duplicate second append writes `&current->registeredServer` at index 1, exactly one pointer past the 8-byte heap buffer. AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 8` at this statement.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_3736 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which replayed the staged 458-byte witness and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 8` in `Service_FindServers` with stack `processMSG -> processSecureChannelMessage -> UA_SecureChannel_finalizeChunk`.

format.name: OPC UA SecureConversation chunk stream
format.contract: The staged witness is exactly 458 bytes long and splits into four chunks with sizes 132, 97, 132, and 97 bytes. The first `MSG` body begins at offset `0x9c` with request-type bytes `01 20 b5 01`, so `processMSG()` dispatches it as numeric id 437 (`RegisterServerRequest_Encoding_DefaultBinary`). Under the staged `UA_decodeBinary` semantics, that request inserts exactly one online registered-server entry whose stored `serverUri` is a zero-length `UA_String`. The second `MSG` body begins at offset `0x181` with request-type bytes `01 20 a6 01`, so `processMSG()` dispatches it as numeric id 422 (`FindServersRequest_Encoding_DefaultBinary`). That request decodes `serverUrisSize = 2`, and both `serverUris` elements become the same zero-length `UA_String`. Because the fresh server's default `applicationUri` is the non-empty literal `urn:unconfigured:application`, both filter entries miss the line-129 self-URI guard and fall into the registered-server loop. In vulnerable `Service_FindServers()`, those exact semantics make the sole registered server match twice while `foundServerFilteredPointer` has capacity for only one pointer, so the second append at line 136 triggers the saved 8-byte heap-buffer-overflow write.
